one_line_contribution: A pre-registered, statistically rigorous audit of how much of a frozen procedural-memory bank's accuracy gain over a hand-written prompt (measured on gpt-oss-120b via ExpeL-style retrieval) survives once a GEPA-optimized instruction sees the same training episodes, formalized as a substitution ratio S tested by a superiority+TOST-equivalence conjunction, with a token-matched compiled-bank arm and a deliberately non-compilable positive control to separate a true null from an underpowered one.
closest_prior_work: EvoAgentBench (arXiv 2607.05202), which the proposal's own collision check names as closest work: it already runs Vanilla, Memento, ReasoningBank, and GEPA on a shared 528/267 train/test split across four domains and three backbones — the exact 'memory vs. optimizer on the same trajectories' table this proposal exists to interrogate, and its headline finding (no automatic method wins in every cell; GEPA nearly matches a curated reference on one backbone) is cited here as motivation rather than as a competing result. What remains genuinely new relative to it is the combined I1xM1/I2xM1/I2xM0 cells, the token-matched compiled-bank arm C, the coverage-matched B_touched control, and the paired substitution-ratio statistics — real additions but incremental completions of an existing table rather than a new comparison in kind, published only two months before this proposal.
strongest_objection: The entire load-bearing test (H1 and H2 on A1) runs on gpt-oss-120b, a 120B-parameter model outside the track's stated resource envelope ('self-hosted inference on open-weight models up to ~32B... The interesting result must not depend on frontier-scale models'). A1 was picked specifically because an internal pilot found a non-null bank effect only there; Qwen3.5-27B (A2), the one agent actually inside the track's model class, is exactly where the bank's effect was null, so it is demoted to a 'degenerate regime' where S is not even computed (prediction 11). The paper's central, falsifiable claim is therefore never tested within the resource/scope boundary this track set for itself, and the agent choice reads as selecting the regime that guarantees a measurable effect rather than the regime the track asked for.
what_would_fix_it: Make the primary, load-bearing grid run on an in-scope agent (7B-32B) where a genuine — even if smaller — bank effect at the hand-written instruction can be pre-registered, rather than making the compliant agent (Qwen3.5-27B) the 'degenerate' side case; add at least one genuinely self-editing memory system (e.g. a ReasoningBank-style online-distillation bank) alongside the frozen, built-once ExpeL bank B, since the track is titled 'Self-Editing Memory' and B/B-dup are static; and cite the internal pilot ('proposal (1)') and the litscan file as verifiable appendices rather than unpublished internal context the agent-selection and gate thresholds depend on.
missing_baseline: A dynamically self-editing memory bank (ReasoningBank-style distillation from self-judged successes/failures, or Mem0/A-MEM-style continual rewriting) is never built or tested; B and the B-dup positive control are constructed once from S_train and then frozen and hashed for the whole study. Given the track's own name and the fact that Related Work section (1) treats ReasoningBank as a peer target system, a reviewer would demand the substitution/compilation result be shown for at least one truly self-editing memory, since as written the finding could be specific to one static, non-self-editing bank-construction method rather than to the class of systems the track is about.
preprint_collision: Unusually rigorous for this genre: a dated fresh scan (2026-09-03), by-id verification for 54 arXiv IDs, and an explicit self-correction of a prior version's erroneous retraction of five citations, including an honest concession that the closest work (EvoAgentBench) already runs the three-way memory/optimizer comparison the earlier proposal draft claimed did not exist. But it is entirely self-reported and unverifiable here, and its own 'Residual risk' paragraph names the exact exposure a reviewer should weight heavily: 'a GEPA + memory ablation may exist in an appendix of a systems paper' — which is precisely the combined cell (I1xM1) claimed as the proposal's chief novel contribution. Given the field's admitted volatility, the check's real weakness is not thinness but the structural blind spot of keyword/HF-Papers scanning against an ablation buried in someone else's appendix or a not-yet-indexed ICLR 2027 submission.
